hints: Focus on what cold dilute versus hot concentrated manganate(VII) does to a C=C double bond, mild addition or full cleavage.

Notice that cis-but-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, gives a diol with two $\text{-OH}$ groups under cold dilute conditions, but gives two molecules of ethanoic acid under hot concentrated conditions.
Recall that sodium metal reacts with any $\text{-OH}$ (alcohol or acid), while sodium hydroxide solution reacts only with the acidic $\text{-COOH}$ group, then check which product has which.
walkthrough:
**Identify product X from mild oxidation**

Cold, dilute acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives syn addition of two $\text{-OH}$ groups across the double bond. It does not break the carbon chain.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 + [O] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$$
So X is butane-2,3-diol, a diol with two alcohol groups.

**Identify product Y from vigorous oxidation**

Hot, concentrated acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ cleaves the C=C bond completely. Each $\text{=CHCH}_3$ fragment is oxidised to a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 + [O] \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
So Y is ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, a carboxylic acid.

**Test with sodium metal**

Sodium is a very strong test for any labile $\text{-OH}$ proton. Both alcohols and carboxylic acids give hydrogen gas.

$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{R-COOH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-COONa} + \text{H}_2$$
So both X (diol) and Y (acid) will react with Na.

**Test with sodium hydroxide solution**

NaOH is a base that neutralises acids but is not strong enough to react with a neutral alcohol. Only carboxylic acids react.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So only Y reacts with NaOH, X does not. That gives both react with Na, only one reacts with NaOH.

options.A: The first half is right, both X and Y react with Na. The second half is wrong because Y is ethanoic acid and acids are neutralised by NaOH to give salt plus water. Saying neither reacts forgets the acidity of a carboxylic acid.
options.B: X is butane-2,3-diol and Y is ethanoic acid. Both contain $\text{-OH}$ protons so both liberate $\text{H}_2$ with Na, but only Y contains $\text{-COOH}$ so only Y is neutralised by NaOH. This matches both react with Na and only one reacts with NaOH.
options.C: This underestimates sodium. Students choosing this think only acids react with Na, but alcohols also react to give alkoxide plus $\text{H}_2$. Both the diol X and the acid Y react, not only one.
options.D: The NaOH part is correct (only Y reacts), but the Na part is wrong. It is a common trap to think Na behaves like NaOH and only reacts with acids. In fact Na reacts with both alcohols and acids, so both X and Y react with Na.
